newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin bank, NordLB must be equal partners-premier.
newsitem.headline: Berlin bank, NordLB must be equal partners-premier.

text.p: The premier of the German state of Lower Saxony, Gerhard Schroeder, said he would only allow a merger between Norddeutsche Landesbank and Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG if the banks were treated as equal partners.
"I will not accept anything without absolute parity," Schroeder told news magazine Der Spiegel in an interview.
Lower Saxony, which owns 40 percent of NordLB, and the state of Berlin, which owns 56.8 percent of Bankgesellschaft, must have commensurate stakes in a merged group, Schroeder said.
He added that the group would have to be based in Hanover as well as Berlin.
Spiegel released the interview ahead of publication in Monday's edition.
Bankgesellschaft said last week it was sure that a tie-up with NordLB was possible, but that a whole range of difficult issues had to be resolved first and that the process would take years.

In a move that fuelled speculation about mergers in Germany's overcrowded banking sector, the two banks last month got the go-ahead from the states that own them to intensify talks about increasing cooperation.
